articles.title: My wife swears by weighted blankets to sleep – and now I understand why
articles.summary: A 10-lb weighted blanket made a short night of sleep feel surprisingly restful – and I have found new uses for it too. Five common sleep problems, solved by experts. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I n 2017, my wife, Tracey, and I bought our first weighted blanket. It was filled with thousands of tiny glass beads sewn into quilted pockets to spread gentle pressure across the body without layering comforters. Tracey grew up in eastern Canada, where piling on blankets and comforters was a perfectly reasonable way to make a bed feel cozy. When we lived in Arizona some eight years ago, the weather made all those layers unbearable.

For Tracey, the weighted blanket was the solution; she’s slept under it for nearly a decade. She noticed a big improvement in her sleep, and her ease helped mine as well. I understood the appeal conceptually, but I didn’t fully grasp the value until I pulled one over me to try to make the most of a short, six-and-a-half-hour night.
I woke up refreshed, having slept straight through until morning, without the grogginess that I usually feel after a night cut short.

articles.title: Location-tracking apps have turned me into a gibbering wreck – but I just can’t look away
articles.summary: When my loved ones are on the move, I can’t rest until I know they’ve got from A to B safely. How I long for the ignorance of the olden days. I’ll call it compassionate surveillance. It’s what I do when I’m worried about a loved one who is on the move. I’m not sure it’s a good thing.
body: I cross my heart and hope to die when I swear to you that I only do this when they are in transit. Honestly, I never look up where they are on a night out or whatever. That would be weird – or weirder, anyway. But when they get in a car, I get the fear. The catastrophising begins. It’s a big world and their car is small. A million other cars, buses and lorries share the roads on which they are motoring. In this, as in all things, overthinking is calamitous. The more you think about what could go wrong, the more your imagination obliges with a steady stream of ghastly possibilities.

The answer is simple: stop being an idiot, stop torturing yourself, stop thinking about it and think about something else. Sometimes, I achieve this. More often, I don’t. I resist the temptation to check the tech for as long as possible, but invariably I give in. I’ve yet to find anything absorbing enough to distract me from the paranoia. I can be sitting at a football match, in a live radio studio, in an intense conversation, and that will work only for a while before a sick feeling strikes and I’m wondering if my loved ones are all right.
points: When my loved ones are on the move, I can’t rest until I know they’ve got from A to B safely.

articles.title: Are you cleaning your cat litter box correctly?
articles.summary: How often should you clean your cat’s litter box? Plus three other tips for peak cat cleanliness. Throughout history, people have revered cats. Ancient Egyptians worshipped feline deities. In Norse mythology, the Viking goddess Freya rode around in a sled pulled by two cats.
body: As anyone who has lived with a cat knows, we serve them and not the other way around. This includes the messy and malodorous task of tending their litter box.

According to experts, there is often room for improvement. “The most common mistake people make when it comes to their cat’s litter is creating a setup that works for them instead of for the cat,” says Samantha Bell, cat expert and content strategist for the non-profit rescue Best Friends Animal Society. “But we bring our cats into our homes, so we need to do our best to ensure they are as comfortable as possible, and a litter box is a huge part of their comfort.”
Below, what you need to know to ensure your feline overlord’s bathroom satisfaction.

On TikTok, I once saw someone claim cat owners should have a litter box in every room. I imagined my small apartment crammed with litter boxes and despaired. “Is that what you want?” I desperately asked my cat, who doesn’t speak English and doesn’t respect me enough to answer me even if she did.

articles.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: pair a little skirt with a chunky jumper for the perfect balancing act
articles.summary: Let your legs enjoy the last of the summer’s breeze while a thick top or jacket keeps away the autumn chill. This is the most enjoyable time of the year to get dressed because clothes can just be clothes.
body: And this benign early part of autumn is more fun to dress for than the equivalent weather in spring, because we still have a bit of summer swagger. The summer habit of wearing shorts and halter tops and even swimwear has gotten us a little loose, a little more laid-back about flashing a bit of skin here or there. It is about more than bare flesh, though. There is something about summer that flexes the flashy dresser in everyone – whether that’s fancy dress for a festival, or just the way that putting on a pair of sunglasses brings out your inner movie star.

It is very important to hold on to that summer glow, that more fabulous version of yourself, the one who starred in your holiday snaps carousel, for as long as you can. I do this literally, getting through my bodyweight in Dove Visible Glow, my preferred slap-it-on-like-body-lotion gradual self-tan, between now and when the clocks go back. But the less literal-minded among you can hold on to that lovely golden-hour feeling in your mind, as well as in your body. Stay locked into your summer playlist and keep hold of that windows-down, shades-on spirit of freedom at least until the leaves start to turn.

articles.title: 9 Pet-Friendly Hotels in Savannah Where Your Dog Gets the Five-Star Treatment
articles.summary: From dog-friendly patios to dedicated pup menus, these Savannah hotels make it easy to bring your four-legged friend along for the ride.
body: I love my dog, but she’s not exactly a great traveler. If she were, one of the first places I'd bring her would be Savannah —a city I visit often from my base in Atlanta —where she could sniff her way through one of the nation’s most beautiful historic cities. Whenever I’m in the Hostess City, I can’t help but notice how welcoming it is to dogs, with pups dotting the lush squares and lounging on restaurant patios at places like the Collins Quarter in Forsyth Park and Foxy Loxy Cafe in the Starland District. Even famed Leopold’s Ice Cream makes special sundaes for furry friends to enjoy alfresco.

It’s no surprise, then, that plenty of hotels in town welcome four-legged guests, too. And bringing your dog doesn’t mean sacrificing luxury or hospitality at the best pet-friendly hotels in Savannah. The properties below pair stylish accommodations and thoughtful service with amenities for pups, easy access to green space, and, in some cases, even special menus. Here are nine pet-friendly hotels in Savannah, GA where your dog can feel right at home.

articles.title: 9 Standout Galapagos Cruises for Sailing the Bucket-List Wildlife Destination
articles.summary: From luxury ships to affordable sailings, family-friendly and solo-traveler-favorites, there’s a cruise in the Galapagos for every type of traveler.
body: An extraordinary archipelago 600 miles off the coast of Ecuador, the Galapagos promise a once-in-a-lifetime travel experience—and many agree there's no better way to visit, than by ship. Unlike the typical island-hopping cruise itinerary you'll find elsewhere, Galapagos Island cruises invite travelers to experience some of the most unspoiled environments on earth. The vessels here are small, too—sometimes accommodating as few as 16 passengers. There are no water parks, Broadway-style shows, or casinos on board. Instead, pristine surroundings, uninhabited islands, and rare wildlife are the featured attractions.

articles.title: Can an Arnault Help Revive Nike?
articles.summary: Alexandre Arnault, an LVMH heir with experience at Moët, Tiffany and Rimowa, has been appointed to Nike’s board as the brand struggles to find its footing on a path forward.
body: Nike has a new board member in Alexandre Arnault, the second son of Bernard Arnault and who is currently the deputy CEO of Moët Hennessy, LVMH’s wines and spirits division.

“Alexandre has earned a reputation for helping iconic global brands evolve, innovate and grow in a changing, complex marketplace,” said Nike executive chair Mark Parker on Wednesday. “As part of our commitment to strong governance and thoughtful board succession, we look for leaders with distinctive experiences, fresh perspectives and a proven ability to create long-term value. Alexandre’s leadership across some of the world’s most respected brands will make him a strong addition to our board.”
Nike’s board of directors has its fair share of blockbuster names — like co-founder Phil Knight, and Apple chair and former CEO Tim Cook — but, until now, none that come from the luxury space.

articles.title: With ‘The Holes,’ Max Wolf Friedlich Punctures Male Loneliness
articles.summary: Friedlich’s “The Holes,” produced by Robert Pattinson, opens at Wild Project in New York’s East Village on September 22.
body: The Holes began as an eighth-grade English assignment. Playwright Max Wolf Friedlich ( Job ) remembers his teacher taking him aside to compliment his work and encourage him to pursue writing. Then he told Friedlich he’d have to call his parents; the play was about barroom cruising.

Almost two decades later, as he prepares to stage a version of that first play at Wild Project in Manhattan’s East Village, Friedlich’s answer to his teacher’s question is simply that he’d grown up in Chelsea. (In those days, “What are those guys doing?” was a typical question his mom would find herself fielding.) “That set the tone for the level of transgressiveness I’m always striving for,” he tells Vogue. “I don’t want to get in trouble, but I do want to push boundaries.”

articles.title: Hoy Is Bringing Night-Market Energy to NYC
articles.summary: This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews. This is the first installment of our series Getting on the Map, presented by Apple Maps.
body: When I spoke with Cyed Adraincem, he apologized for stumbling over any words; he’d been up at 4 a.m. to wash the sidewalk in front of his forthcoming restaurant. “I wanted to beat all the foot traffic,” he said.

Adraincem seems to have brought that same dedication to outfitting Hoy, which will serve Filipino street food in a Manila night-market-like space. Though not yet open, the restaurant has already garnered a lot of attention for its loud and off-kilter aesthetic, smart pop cultural ties, and behind-the-scenes peeks into R&D. I asked him about designing the space, the merch plan, and how opening is going.

Cyed Adraincem: It’s Filipino street food, super fast casual. I’m trying to introduce Filipino food to a broader audience because I feel like we’re underrepresented in New York City. We’ll be serving barbecue skewers, lumpia, and a couple different sandwiches. It’s a pretty simple menu, nothing too fancy, mostly traditional, with chef techniques that we’ve learned over the years. I think the New York dining scene wants something more casual, more affordable right now. They don’t want something pretentious; they just want to eat and have a good drink.

articles.title: Can Snap’s Evan Spiegel Sell You a Computer for Your Face?
articles.summary: Smart glasses have gotten more stylish and covert, but Snap’s Specs are an exception. CEO Spiegel thinks that’s their competitive advantage.
body: Silicon Valley has spent the past year stealing from fashion’s playbook, leaning on brand collaborators and fashion ambassadors to make its controversial AI smart glasses look less techie and more stylish. See Meta’s latest AI glasses, which have gotten smaller and more similar to normal spectacles over time. But Snap CEO Evan Spiegel is taking a different approach: doubling down on the tech itself, and betting that Snap’s new Specs AR glasses can establish an aesthetic that gains a cultural credibility of its own.

The glasses, which have been in the works for 11 years, officially launched on Wednesday — the culmination of five previous generations of Spectacles, including two generations of AR prototypes released to developers in 2021 and 2024. Designed in-house with a much bulkier, heavier construction than ordinary glasses, Specs look like a tech product first, accessory second.

body: Kitted out in no less than three eye-popping rings, pear-shaped drop earrings, a Happy Sport watch, and a never-seen-before pendant with seven dancing diamonds, Hadid arrived shortly after 9 p.m. A crowd that had formed on the terrace parted ways and hundreds of flashbulbs and iPhones promptly sprung into action. Reunited with Scheufele for the first time since Cannes Film Festival, Hadid twirled, air-kissed, and curtseyed with the co-president and artistic director of the house. “I’m delighted to be here because, not only is it the 50th anniversary of the Happy Diamonds, it is also the 50th anniversary of Chopard in America,” Scheufele told Vogue.
